Calculate the electrical resistivity of a wire.
The wire length is 0.492 m.
The wire diameter is 1.944 mm, which is 0.001944 m.
Use the formula A = πd² for the circular cross-sectional area, with no factor of one quarter.
Compute A = π × (0.001944)² ≈ 1.18713 × 10⁻⁵ m².
The wire resistance is 11.705 Ω.
Use the relation R = ρL/A to solve for resistivity: ρ = RA/L.
Compute ρ = (11.705 × 1.18713 × 10⁻⁵) / 0.492 ≈ 2.824 × 10⁻⁴ Ω·m.
Report the final resistivity in Ω·m with appropriate significant figures, approximately 2.82 × 10⁻⁴ Ω·m.
